title: 27 Men Vanished Off Florida in One Night
sources: U.S. Naval History and Heritage Command, H-Gram 057-4, 'The Disappearance of Flight 19 and Training 49, 5 December 1945': five TBM Avenger torpedo bombers with 14 men (6 Navy, 8 Marines) left NAS Fort Lauderdale on a navigation training flight; flight leader LT Charles Taylor radioed that both his compasses were out and believed he was over the Florida Keys; PBM-5 Mariner 'Training 49' left NAS Banana River with 13 men to search and was never heard from after 7:30 PM; tanker SS Gaines Mills reported flames and an explosion on the water around 7:50 PM; a five-day search found no confirmed wreckage of any of the aircraft
History.com, 'The Mysterious Disappearance of Flight 19' (Evan Andrews)
Smithsonian Magazine, 'How the Disappearance of Flight 19 Fueled the Legend of the Bermuda Triangle'

lines.text: Five Navy bombers took off, and not one was ever found.

lines.text: Fourteen men, on a training flight.
Then the leader radioed, both my compasses are out.
He thought he was over the Florida Keys.
But that's not the strangest part.
A rescue plane went after them, with thirteen men,

lines.text: A passing ship saw flames on the water.
Twenty-seven men, gone in one night,
and the sea never gave back a single piece of those
